issue_context.title: Support for Hashtag Custom Filters
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Create a custom filter for `#example` and apply the Whole Word option
2. Create a status with the text `"Test filter https://example.org/#example test"`
4. Fetch the custom filters with `CustomFilter.cached_filters_for("<account id>")`
5. Apply the filters to the created status: `CustomFilter.apply_cached_filters(filters, status)`



### Expected behaviour

The filter should not match because "https://example.org/#example" is not including "#example" at a word boundary

### Actual behaviour

Filter matches the hash fragment in the URL

### Detailed description

It seems this bug is introduced by the logic of the whole word filter application:

```ruby
sb = /\A[[:word:]]/.match?(keyword.keyword) ? '\b' : ''
eb = /[[:word:]]\z/.match?(keyword.keyword) ? '\b' : ''

/(?mix:#{sb}#{Regexp.escape(keyword.keyword)}#{eb})/
```

Where `/\A[[:word:]]/` does not match on symbols (e.g., it'll return false for "#example")

This results in the word boundaries not being respected.

### Mastodon instance

_No response_

### Mastodon version

main

### Technical details

If this is happening on your own Mastodon server, please fill out those:
- Ruby version: 3.2.2
- Node.js version: 20.9
comments:
I was going to write a test case, but it appears that we may have zero code coverage of this area of the code?
cc @renchap / @ClearlyClaire

I think the solution is to actually match as follows:
```ruby
sb = /\A|^[[:word:]]/.match?(keyword.keyword) ? '\b' : ''
eb = /[[:word:]]\z|$/.match?(keyword.keyword) ? '\b' : ''

/(?mix:#{sb}#{Regexp.escape(keyword.keyword)}#{eb})/
```

That is, match on start of word or on start of line and end of word or end of line
An alternative solution would be the introduction of custom filters specifically for hashtags, as noted in: https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/discussions/21762

review_comments: This is likely not the most ideal way to test this, but it was one of the tests I could find for custom filters, there didn't actually seem to be tests directly for custom filters.

Whilst this does work, we may actually want to use the logic that the streaming server uses here, which is "If the filter starts with or end with non-whitespace, do a boundary match"

```suggestion
            sb = /^[\S]/.match?(keyword.keyword) ? '\b' : ''
            eb = /[\S]$/.match?(keyword.keyword) ? '\b' : ''
```

It seems ruby's \A and \z do not match symbols, only alphanumerical characters.
